scenario: Draft includes a byline reading 'Jane Ortiz, RN, 8 years in clinical nutrition' linked to a full author profile page listing her credentials, plus `author` schema pointing to a Person entity matching the visible name.
A product-testing article states exactly what was tested, the 6-week test period, and the conditions used, and uses first-person language like 'we measured battery life daily for six weeks.'
Every statistic in the post links directly to the original government report or peer-reviewed study that produced the number, with inline citations next to each claim.
The post includes a proprietary survey of 500 customers the company ran itself, and calls it out in a clearly labeled 'Our original survey data' callout box separate from third-party stats.
The article shows both a 'Published on' date and a 'Last updated' date matching the page's dateModified schema, and links to the site's corrections policy after a recent factual fix.
The post is published under a generic 'Team' byline with no name, no credentials, and no link to any author or About page, on a topic (medical dosing) where reader trust depends on who is speaking.
A glowing product review does not disclose that the reviewer's company has an affiliate revenue relationship with the product being reviewed, and never states how the review was actually conducted.
The post cites 'studies show productivity increases by 40%' with a link to another blog's recap article, never linking to the original study or dataset behind the number.

The article mixes the company's own unpublished internal test results into the same sentence and formatting as a third-party industry statistic, with no labeling distinguishing original data from cited data.
The page was silently edited to fix a factual error discovered by a reader, with no visible 'last updated' date change, no mention of the correction, and no link to any corrections policy.
violates_gate: 5. Trust signals: last-updated dates and correction policy

scenario: The pre-publish checklist is skipped entirely: no author bio check, no primary-source verification, and no confirmation that the visible dates match structured data before the post goes live.
